label: Burkitt in disguise: clonal transformation of incidentally detected gallbladder diffuse large B-cell lymphoma in a liver transplant recipient.
summary: Post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorders (PTLDs) typically arise months to years after solid-organ transplantation and are frequently driven by Epstein-Barr virus (EBV). However, EBV-negative monomorphic PTLDs are increasingly recognized as an alternative pathogenesis. We report a case of a 64-year-old man who underwent liver transplantation and was found to have a minute focus of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) in the resected gallbladder.
